facts.value: Town of Clay Local Law No. 6 of 2026; the Department of State index number is also 6 of 2026.
facts.locator: Physical page 1, cover and office-use box
facts.supporting_quote: Local Law Number ... 6 of the year 2026; Department of State Local Law Index Number: 6 of the year 2026

facts.value: The cover describes a 12-month moratorium concerning large-scale data centers, AI computing facilities, cryptocurrency mining and similar high-intensity computing uses. The title text is visibly struck through; “SEE ATTACHED” appears below it.
facts.supporting_quote: Temporary Moratorium for twelve (12) months ... large-scale data centers, artificial intelligence (AI) computing facilities, cryptocurrency mining operations and similar high-intensity computing uses ... SEE ATTACHED

facts.value: The cover bears a Department of State, State Records filing stamp dated July 6, 2026.
facts.supporting_quote: FILED / STATE RECORDS / JUL 06 2026 / DEPARTMENT OF STATE

facts.value: The completed final-adoption paragraph certifies that Local Law No. 6 of 2026 was passed by the Town Board on June 29, 2026. The municipality-name blank in that paragraph is unfilled.
facts.supporting_quote: Final adoption by local legislative body only ... local law number 6 of 2026 ... was duly passed by the TOWN BOARD on June 29 2026

facts.value: The transcript certification is signed and dated July 1, 2026. Its blank for the paragraph number remains unfilled.
facts.locator: Physical page 3, certification and signature line
facts.supporting_quote: I further certify that I have compared the preceding local law with the original ... and was finally adopted in the manner indicated in the paragraph _____ above. ... July 1, 2026

facts.value: The attached law identifies itself as Town of Clay Local Law No. 6 of 2026 and describes a six-month moratorium on new zoning requests or special permits related to solar battery storage systems.
facts.supporting_quote: LOCAL LAW #6 of 2026 ... a six (6) month moratorium prohibiting the application or approval of any new zoning requests or special permits related to solar battery storage systems.

facts.value: The operative text provides a six-month moratorium on Town Board land-use decisions related to solar battery storage systems in Clay.
facts.supporting_quote: As of the effective date of this local law there will be a six (6) month moratorium on all Town Board land use decisions related to solar battery storage systems in Clay.

facts.value: The attached solar-battery law states that it takes effect immediately upon filing with the Secretary of State and becomes null and void six months after filing unless extended or terminated by the Town Board.
facts.supporting_quote: This Local Law shall take effect immediately upon filing with the Secretary of State. ... This local law shall become null and void six (6) months after filing, unless extended or terminated by the Town Board.

facts.value: The clerk’s letter is dated June 30, 2026 and certifies a resolution passed at a special Town Board meeting held June 29, 2026.
facts.locator: Physical page 6, date and opening paragraph
facts.supporting_quote: June 30, 2026 ... the Special Meeting of the Town Board ... held on June 29, 2026

facts.value: The letter’s subject line names the Town of Clay Battery Energy Storage System Law, but its body describes resolutions concerning a 12-month moratorium on specified computing uses.
facts.locator: Physical page 6, subject line and resolution paragraphs
facts.supporting_quote: RE: Approved Resolution – Local Law No. 6 of the year 2026 (Town of Clay Battery Energy Storage System Law) ... Temporary Moratorium for a period of 12-months ... large-scale data centers, artificial intelligence (“AI”) computing facilities, cryptocurrency mining operations, and similar high-intensity computing uses

facts.value: The letter reports that Deputy Supervisor Bick moved both an environmental resolution, seconded by Councilor Capria, and the computing-moratorium approval resolution, seconded by Councilor Russell.
facts.supporting_quote: Deputy Supervisor Bick moved ... does not require the preparation of an EIS. Motion was seconded by Councilor Capria. ... Deputy Supervisor Bick moved ... Motion was seconded by Councilor Russell.

facts.value: The letter lists Courtney Gauthier, Ryan Russell, David Capria, Ed Wisnowski, Eugene Young and Joseph Bick as voting in favor, and states that the resolution was adopted.
facts.supporting_quote: Courtney Gauthier - in favor; Ryan Russell - in favor; David Capria - in favor; Ed Wisnowski - in favor; Eugene Young - in favor; Joseph Bick - in favor. The Resolution was thereupon duly adopted.

uncertainties: The cover, attached law and clerk’s letter contain conflicting descriptions of Local Law No. 6. The source does not resolve the instrument’s identity.
The attached solar-battery law’s effective and termination clauses cannot be attributed to the computing moratorium described in the clerk’s letter.
The source does not establish a coherent filed computing law, an exact endpoint for a computing moratorium, or its current force.
